title: Blistered Cherry Tomatoes
summary: Cherry tomatoes charred in a hot pan until they split and turn jammy, with garlic, chili, and a splash of vinegar. A bright, acidic topping for rich bowls.

ingredients.note: or leftover fat from browned sausage

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat the oil in cast iron over medium-high until it shimmers. A pan that just browned sausage works well.

steps.title: Blister without stirring
steps.text: Add the tomatoes in a single layer and leave them alone until the bottoms char and skins start to split. Work in batches if needed; crowded tomatoes steam instead of blistering.

steps.title: Shake and finish
steps.text: Shake the pan and cook until most are blistered and a few have burst and gone jammy.

steps.title: Garlic and chili
steps.text: Add the garlic and chili flakes for the last minute only, so the garlic turns golden without burning.

steps.title: Season off the heat
steps.text: Take off the heat and stir in the salt, vinegar, and herbs.

notes: Blistering concentrates the sugar and removes the raw, watery texture, so this wins over tomato skeptics more often than raw tomatoes do. Serve in a bowl on the table rather than on every plate, and make sure each bowl gets a few of the burst ones; those are the sweetest. Good spooned over mac and cheese with browned Italian sausage.
